note: A low, constant worry about falling behind. It's everywhere now, in 容貌焦虑 and 中年焦虑, and you feel it as pressure from the whole world around you.
To bring two people or parties together. You picture the matchmaker's red thread, and 牵线搭桥 sounds like a favour someone will remember doing for you.
To die suddenly, often blamed on overwork. You hear it about young programmers and couriers, and it brings a chill when you check how late you've been staying up.
Knowing you've lost on the merits. You go quiet because your 理, your reason, has run short, even if nobody has said so yet.

gloss: (idiom) bored to death; bored stiff; overcome with boredom
note: Bored and listless, with nothing to hold on to. You feel the emptiness of an afternoon with nothing to do, and it's a bookish way to say it.
To scheme against someone. You feel a chill at 被人算计: someone has quietly arranged things behind your back while smiling at you.
To win people over with favours. You picture a halter going gently on a horse, so there's always some suspicion about what the kindness is for.
A professional rank in China's state system, like senior engineer or associate professor. You know teachers and doctors chase it for years, because pay and respect hang on it.
To show off and put yourself forward. Saying someone 爱表现 is a mild dig: you picture them making sure the boss has noticed.

gloss: to arrange a fight with sb
note: To arrange a fight by appointment. It borrows 约 from making a date, so it sounds almost comic, like teenagers or online rivals agreeing a time and place.
Voluntary, at least officially. You may smile at 自愿加班 or 自愿捐款, because in an organisation you know that not volunteering can get noticed.
